messages:
james: Heads up — customer ACME filed an escalation: intermittent 401s and reports missing audit log entries around 2026-03-05 03:15-03:45 UTC. They mentioned a KMS/HSM rotation briefly. Paging sec/oncall/infra.

mike: oncall here. I saw a 401 spike 03:22-03:40 UTC. Token validation service returned 401s; I rolled back an auth config change at 03:30 to stop the spike. Need audit writes to confirm customer-facing gaps.

olivia: Are we sure missing logs are from retention policy vs write failures during rotation? We need scope before deciding notifications.

sarah: quick status: we performed a scheduled HSM key rotation at ~03:20. Rotation completed normally but a subset of writes to the audit-ingest pipeline failed due to a brief DNS resolution issue to audit-ingest.service. Hypothesis: failed writes + delayed retries = visible gaps. Investigating replay/backfill.

james: Customer wants timeline and to know if PII or plaintext keys were exposed. They also asked whether we'll notify all affected orgs or only ACME.

mike: Clarifying question — were any decrypted values accessible? We use envelope encryption; HSM keys are not exportable. No sign yet of plaintext leakage, but I'll validate access logs.

sarah: Confirmed: HSM policy prevents key export. No evidence of key material egress. We still need to audit IAM and KMS access logs to be 100% sure.

olivia: From a compliance perspective: if audit entries were lost within the retention window, policy says we may need to notify customers and regulators. What's our customer notification SLA for integrity/retention incidents? My read: 72 hours.

sarah: Policy check: yes, notify impacted customers within 72 hours for incidents affecting data integrity or availability. I'm drafting a notification template now — will include timeline, scope, mitigations, and remediation steps. Need confirmed scope list first.

mike: Running quick query to enumerate orgs with failed acked writes during window:
```
select org_id, count(*) as failed_writes
from audit_writes
where ts >= '2026-03-05T03:15:00Z' and ts <= '2026-03-05T03:45:00Z' and status != 'acked'
group by org_id;
```
I'll paste results shortly.

security-bot: Incident created: SEC-2026-142 — severity P2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/SEC-2026-142

james: :thumbsup: include Legal and Customer Success on the notification. CS will coordinate outreach and any compensatory steps.

olivia: Also cc Data Protection Officer — if logs contain user identifiers we need to follow GDPR notification guidance.

sarah: Action plan I'm proposing: 1) Mike to produce org-level failed-write list (owner: mike) 2) Attempt replay/backfill from write buffer for affected orgs (owner: infra) 3) Legal + CS to review notification draft and approve wording (owner: legal/cs) 4) Post-mortem with remediation items and ETA. Draft notification by EOD.

mike: Query results: A123 -> 84 failed writes; B456 -> 12 failed writes. Uploaded CSV (sensitive) to secure share: https://internal.redwood/s/incident/SEC-2026-142/data.csv

olivia: Thanks — retention checks show both orgs' logs are still within retention window. We should offer to attempt replay and restore where possible.

sarah: Replay update: A123 replay success (all events re-ingested). B456 replay partial: 9/12 successfully re-ingested; 3 events still missing. Investigating why those 3 not present in buffer.

james: Legal, please advise on the exact phrasing re: "no plaintext key export" — we should be careful to avoid absolute statements until audit is complete.

mike: Infra will add a prioritized backfill job for B456 and surface any missing raw blobs. ETA initial attempt by 02:00 UTC tomorrow.

sarah: Draft notification outline: what happened, time window, affected orgs (A123, B456), mitigation (replayed A123, partial for B456), next steps, contact. Proposed remediation list: add validation after KMS rotations, stronger DNS/ingest retries, alerting on any unrecoverable audit-writes. ETA for full remediation delivery: 5 days.

olivia: Make sure notification contains exact timeframe and a point of contact for privacy questions. Also include whether backups were used and the replay success rate.

james: I'll coordinate CS outreach once Legal okays the draft. Keep updates here; escalate to #all-hands if severity changes.

sarah: Will post the notification draft here when ready. Also opening a dedicated postmortem doc and assigning follow-ups.

mike: final quick note — no evidence of keys leaving HSM or plaintext exfiltration per current logs. We'll include HSM audit timeline in the report.

sarah: thanks everyone. Next update in ~2 hours or when we have full replay results.
